what: SouthState is a bank across the American Southeast, lending to businesses and households from Florida to Texas, and it runs a large correspondent banking business serving other banks.
customers: Businesses and households in Florida, the Carolinas, Georgia, Alabama, Virginia and Texas.
money: commercial and consumer lending funded by deposits
interest rate and bond services for other banks
moat: A deposit base across the fastest-growing states in America, plus a correspondent business serving hundreds of smaller banks that would be hard for a newcomer to win.
risks: Commercial real estate concentration, as with most Southeastern banks
The Independent Financial merger has to be integrated
Deposit costs rise quickly when rates rise
opportunities: 10.7 times earnings with a 29.8% net margin and $1.5B of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $1.7B to $2.7B last year as the Texas merger came in
Analysts see about 20% upside, and its states keep gaining population and businesses
watch: Loan growth and credit quality in the newly acquired Texas book.
